question_text: Which of the following actions can be grouped as a pull? (निम्नलिखित में से किस क्रिया को खिंचाव के रूप में समूहीकृत किया जा सकता है?)
options: Hitting a cricket ball (क्रिकेट की गेंद को मारना)
Kicking a football (फ़ुटबॉल को लात मारना)
Opening a drawer (दराज खोलना)
Pushing a heavy box (भारी बक्से को धक्का देना)
explanation: A pull is a force that brings an object closer to the person applying it. When you open a drawer, you apply force towards yourself, hence it is a pull. (खिंचाव वह बल है जो किसी वस्तु को बल लगाने वाले व्यक्ति के करीब लाता है।)
distractor_rationale: Hitting, kicking, and pushing all involve moving an object away from the person, which are examples of a push, not a pull.

ai_context.learning_goal: Identify the basic nature of force as a push or pull.
common_misconceptions: Students often confuse pulling an object with lifting an object.
ai_context.hint: Think about whether the action brings the object closer to you or moves it away.

question_text: Why do school bags have wide straps? (स्कूल बैग में चौड़ी पट्टियाँ क्यों होती हैं?)
options: To increase the pressure on shoulders (कंधों पर दबाव बढ़ाने के लिए)
To make the bag look attractive (बैग को आकर्षक बनाने के लिए)
To decrease the pressure on shoulders by increasing area (क्षेत्रफल बढ़ाकर कंधों पर दबाव कम करने के लिए)
To reduce the weight of the bag (बैग का वजन कम करने के लिए)
answer: To decrease the pressure on shoulders by increasing area (क्षेत्रफल बढ़ाकर कंधों पर दबाव कम करने के लिए)
explanation: Pressure is inversely proportional to area (Pressure = Force / Area). Wide straps have a larger area, which distributes the weight of the bag (force) over a larger part of the shoulder, thus decreasing the pressure. (दबाव क्षेत्रफल के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है। चौड़ी पट्टियाँ वजन को बड़े हिस्से में फैलाती हैं, जिससे दबाव कम होता है।)
distractor_rationale: Narrow straps would increase pressure. The straps don't change the actual weight of the bag, only how the force is distributed.

ai_context.learning_goal: Apply the mathematical relationship between pressure, force, and area to a real-life scenario.
common_misconceptions: Students might think wide straps reduce the actual weight of the bag rather than just reducing pressure.
ai_context.hint: Recall the formula for pressure. If the area (A) gets larger, what happens to the pressure (P)?

question_text: A ball rolling on the ground gradually slows down and stops. Which force is responsible for this? (जमीन पर लुढ़कती हुई एक गेंद धीरे-धीरे धीमी होकर रुक जाती है। इसके लिए कौन सा बल जिम्मेदार है?)
options: Magnetic force (चुंबकीय बल)
Muscular force (पेशीय बल)
Electrostatic force (स्थिरवैद्युत बल)
Frictional force (घर्षण बल)
explanation: The force of friction always acts in the opposite direction to the motion of an object, slowing it down. It is a contact force between the ball and the ground. (घर्षण बल हमेशा किसी वस्तु की गति की विपरीत दिशा में कार्य करता है, जो उसे धीमा कर देता है।)
distractor_rationale: Magnetic and electrostatic forces are non-contact and don't apply here. Muscular force was used to start the motion but doesn't stop it.

ai_context.learning_goal: Identify frictional force as the cause of slowing down of objects.
common_misconceptions: Students often believe that if no force is applied, an object naturally stops on its own, not realizing friction IS a force.
ai_context.hint: Which invisible force opposes motion when two surfaces are touching?

question_text: Leaves fall down from a tree to the ground. Which type of force is acting on the leaves? (पत्तियाँ पेड़ से ज़मीन पर गिरती हैं। पत्तियों पर किस प्रकार का बल कार्य कर रहा है?)
options: Gravitational force (गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल)
Frictional force (घर्षण बल)
Magnetic force (चुंबकीय बल)
Muscular force (पेशीय बल)
explanation: The earth pulls every object towards itself. This pull is an attractive, non-contact force known as the force of gravity. (पृथ्वी हर वस्तु को अपनी ओर खींचती है, जिसे गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल कहा जाता है।)
distractor_rationale: Friction opposes motion. Magnetic force only affects magnetic materials. Muscular force requires physical exertion.

ai_context.learning_goal: Recognize gravity as a universal non-contact force.
common_misconceptions: Students might confuse gravity with magnetism.
ai_context.hint: What is the force that pulls everything towards the Earth without physically touching them?

question_text: A rubber sucker pressed on a smooth surface sticks to it. Why? (एक चिकनी सतह पर दबाया गया रबर शोषक (sucker) उस पर चिपक जाता है। क्यों?)
options: Due to the gravitational force acting on it (इस पर कार्य करने वाले गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल के कारण)
Because atmospheric pressure outside is greater than the pressure inside (क्योंकि बाहर का वायुमंडलीय दबाव अंदर के दबाव से अधिक होता है)
Because the sucker exerts a magnetic force (क्योंकि शोषक चुंबकीय बल लगाता है)
Because the surface attracts the rubber (क्योंकि सतह रबर को आकर्षित करती है)
answer: Because atmospheric pressure outside is greater than the pressure inside (क्योंकि बाहर का वायुमंडलीय दबाव अंदर के दबाव से अधिक होता है)
explanation: When you press the sucker, most of the air between its cup and the surface escapes out. The sucker sticks to the surface because the pressure of atmosphere acts on it from the outside, holding it tightly in place. (जब शोषक को दबाया जाता है, तो अंदर की हवा निकल जाती है और बाहर का वायुमंडलीय दबाव उसे चिपका कर रखता है।)
distractor_rationale: Gravity pulls downwards, not against the surface. Rubber is non-magnetic. Surfaces don't naturally attract rubber.

ai_context.learning_goal: Evaluate the effects of atmospheric pressure in a practical scenario.
common_misconceptions: Students think the rubber sucker is 'sticky' on its own or uses a vacuum 'force' to pull itself, rather than external air pushing it down.
ai_context.hint: Think about what happens to the air underneath the sucker when you press it down, and how the air outside reacts.
